content: Haemophilus b capsular polysaccharide, which is derived from Haemophilus b Conjugate Vaccines, has been detected in the urine of some individuals who have received the vaccine. As a result, urine antigen detection tests may not provide reliable diagnostic information for suspected Haemophilus influenzae type b (H. influenzae type b) infections within one to two weeks following the administration of an H. influenzae type b-containing vaccine, such as HIBERIX. In clinical studies, a booster dose of HIBERIX was administered at the same time as one of the following vaccines: DTaP, DTaP-IPV, DTaP-HBV-IPV, or DTaP-HBV. It is important to note that these formulations were non-U.S. versions of the vaccines, which contained 2.5 mg of 2-phenoxyethanol per dose as a preservative. These non-U.S. formulations correspond to the U.S.-licensed vaccines INFANRIX, KINRIX, and PEDIARIX. Additionally, the dosing regimens for DTaP-IPV and DTaP-HBV-IPV used in these studies are not approved in the United States. Currently, there is insufficient data to confirm whether the immune responses to other vaccines administered at the same time as HIBERIX are unaffected. If HIBERIX is given alongside other injectable vaccines, they should be administered using separate syringes and injected at different anatomical sites. HIBERIX must not be mixed with any other vaccine in the same syringe or vial. Immunosuppressive therapies, such as irradiation, antimetabolites, alkylating agents, cytotoxic drugs, and corticosteroids (when used at doses exceeding physiological levels), may diminish the immune response to HIBERIX.
